PARDS: the PALICC-2 definition

Definition · 2023
Age: from term birth to young adulthood
Timing: within 7 days of a known insult
Imaging: new opacities, not explained by atelectasis or effusion
Origin: not primarily cardiac failure or fluid overload
Oxygenation: OI ≥ 4 or OSI ≥ 5 invasive; S/F ≤ 250 on NIV
PALICC-2, Pediatr Crit Care Med 2023
Join late?ARDSW

How sick is the lung?

Severity · OI = MAP × FiO₂ × 100 ÷ PaO₂
< 8Mild
8–16Moderate
≥ 16Severe
Invasive: oxygenation index
Non-invasive: SpO₂ ÷ FiO₂
PALICC-2 2023

The stiff lung on the screen

Volume control
VC · same VT, stiff lung
High plateau, small peak–plateau gap
Flow reaches zero: no trapping
Volume returns: no leak
The lung, not the airway
Join late?ARDSW

Stress index: the shape of the pressure rise

Volume control · constant flow · passive
Index 1 · linear
Index > 1 · bends up
Index < 1 · bends down
01Straight rise: index 1, just right
02Bends up: > 1.1, overdistension: less PEEP
03Bends down: < 0.9, recruitment: more PEEP
04Read only the inspiratory slope
Grasso, Crit Care Med 2004 · Terragni 2013

PEEP titration · a starting point

The ARDSNet tables

ARDSNet 2000 · ALVEOLI 2004
Lower PEEP · FiO₂0.30.40.40.50.50.60.70.70.70.80.90.90.91.0
Lower PEEP · PEEP558810101012141414161818–24
Higher PEEP · FiO₂0.30.30.30.30.30.40.40.50.50.5–0.80.80.91.01.0
Higher PEEP · PEEP58101214141616182022222224
Read across: the FiO₂ she needs gives the least PEEP to pair with it.
Our girl at FiO₂ 1.0: the lower table says 18–24. Her best compliance was at 12.
PALICC-2: use the table or higher, then titrate to compliance, oxygenation and the blood pressure.

The PEEP staircase

Decremental titration · Boriosi 2011
PC, ΔP fixed at 15
PEEP up by 2 to 20
Then down, reading compliance
Stop 2 above the best
Watch BP and SpO₂ throughout
Boriosi, Pediatr Crit Care Med 2011

R/I ratio: set it up

Recruitment-to-inflation · before the test
Volume assist-control, passive patient, no leak
Test airway closure first: note the AOP
High PEEP ≥ 5 above AOP, held 5–10 min, plateau < 30
Rate 6–8 so every breath empties
Plateau from a 0.3 s pause setting, never a manual hold
rtmaven.com/ri-ratio · Chen et al, AJRCCM 2020
Join late?ARDSW
Our girl · before and after the titration

Dead space fraction

Calculate
AVDSf = (PaCO2 − EtCO2) ÷ PaCO2Alveolar dead space fraction: the share of ventilated alveoli that get no blood flow.Bohr–Enghoff (physiological): (PaCO₂ − PēCO₂) ÷ PaCO₂, with mixed expired CO₂ from volumetric capnography.Recruiting PEEP lowers it; over-distending PEEP raises it again. A high dead space fraction marks a sicker child (Ghuman, PCCM 2012).
PEEPPaCO₂EtCO₂AVDSfResult
65036(50 − 36) ÷ 500.28
125045(50 − 45) ÷ 500.10
PaCO₂ 50 on both gases; EtCO₂ from the titration sheet at the PEEP 6 and PEEP 12 steps. Same rate.

Five ways to injure

Ventilator-induced lung injury
Volutrauma · atelectrauma · barotrauma · biotrauma
Ergotrauma: mechanical power, energy per minute
Power = pressure × volume × rate × flow
Driving pressure × rate is the part you can change
PALICC-2: power is a research measure, not a target
Gattinoni 2016 · PALICC-2 2023

Case 1 · 2-year-old girl · 10 kg

What to keep

Debrief
  1. NIV is a trial with a stop rule. Write the failure criteria down before you start.
  2. Intubation in ARDS is a resuscitation: fluids, pressor and a cuffed tube ready.
  3. Any mode works. The limits are what matter: VT 6–8 mL/kg, plateau ≤ 28–30, driving pressure ≤ 15.
  4. Oxygenation = FiO₂ + mean airway pressure. PEEP first, then inspiratory time, both checked against the flow scalar.
  5. Titrate PEEP to best compliance or lowest driving pressure, and watch the blood pressure.
  6. Asynchrony: check the tube, secretions and chest first, then sedation, then the briefest paralysis.
  7. Outside the ventilator: fluids, infection, haemoglobin, haemodynamics, abdomen, chest wall.
  8. Rescue ladder: prone → HFOV → ECMO discussion. Accept SpO₂ 88–92% and a high CO₂ with pH ≥ 7.20.

What to keep

Debrief
  1. Intubation in asthma is a clinical decision: exhaustion and altered mental state, not a gas.
  2. Ketamine, a cuffed tube, fluid first, pressor ready. Expect hypotension when positive pressure starts.
  3. Low rate, small VT, I:E 1:4, expiratory time 4–5 s, plateau < 30, pH > 7.2.
  4. Peak − plateau is resistance; plateau − PEEP is stretch. Watch the plateau.
  5. External PEEP at or just below the intrinsic PEEP once he triggers; never above it.
  6. Sudden collapse: disconnect first, then DOPE. Ultrasound before the X-ray.
  7. Prevent auto-PEEP: long expiration, bronchodilators, sedation, low VT. Blockade shortest and lowest.

Judge by the patient

PALICC-2: diagnosing PARDS

Pathophysiology
Invasive ventilation: OI ≥ 4 or OSI ≥ 5. Severity is re-graded 4 hours after diagnosis: OI ≥ 16 or OSI ≥ 12 is severe.

Possible and at-risk PARDS

Pathophysiology
On nasal CPAP, bilevel or high-flow: P/F ≤ 300 or S/F ≤ 250 is possible PARDS. Any oxygen to keep SpO₂ ≥ 88% without meeting it: at risk.

What goes wrong

Pathophysiology
Exudative · days 0–7Alveolar–capillary barrier injuredProtein-rich oedema floods the alveoliSurfactant lost: units collapseNeutrophils, cytokines, hyaline membranes
Proliferative · days 7–21Type II cells repair the liningOedema clears if the injury stopsCompliance starts to recover
Fibrotic · beyond 3 weeksScarring in someStiff, poorly recruitable lungDead space and PH rise
At the bedsideShunt: hypoxaemia that oxygen will not fixDead space: CO₂ climbsLow compliance: the baby lungHigh PVR: the RV struggles

Shunt: blood past a closed alveolus

Pathophysiology
A: ventilated and perfused. B: collapsed or flooded, still perfused. The blood leaves without oxygen; more FiO₂ cannot reach it. Recruitment and PEEP can.

Dead space: air with no blood

Pathophysiology
A: ventilated and perfused. B: ventilated, no blood flow (microthrombi, over-distension squeezing the capillaries). The breath is wasted; CO₂ rises and the EtCO₂ gap widens.

The baby lung

Pathophysiology
The same tidal volume goes into far fewer open alveoli: functionally 16 mL/kg to each open unit. Scale the breath to the open lung, not to the child.

Interdependence and shear strain

Pathophysiology
Open alveoli pull on their collapsed neighbours. At the edge of a collapsed unit the stress multiplies: the stress raisers where injury starts. Keeping the lung open evenly protects it.

Where the ventilator hurts

Mechanisms of injury
Volutrauma: overstretch of the open units
Atelectrauma: units opening and closing every breath
Barotrauma: air outside the alveolus
Biotrauma: cytokines from the lung to other organs
Dreyfuss 1988 · Slutsky & Tremblay 1998 · Gattinoni 2016

Strain: how much you stretch

Strain = VT ÷ aerated lung
Strain = VT ÷ aerated lung (FRC)
Child: 6 mL/kg into 30 → 0.2
Baby lung one third → 0.6
Same breath, three times the stretch
Harmful above 1.5–2
Gattinoni · Chiumello, AJRCCM 2008

Stress: the pressure the lung feels

Stress = Paw − Ppl
Stress = transpulmonary pressure
Stress ≈ 12 × strain (specific elastance)
Plateau is the surrogate we read
Stiff chest wall: allow plateau 29–32
Strain 2 ≈ stress 24–27: the ceiling
Chiumello, AJRCCM 2008 · PALICC-2

Why 15 matters

Amato, NEJM 2015 · 3562 adults
ΔPBest predictor of survival
15cmH₂O threshold
VT, PEEPOnly helped via ΔP

Recap · The injured lung

Part 1
Severity by oxygenation index: OI = MAP × FiO₂ × 100 ÷ PaO₂ · SpO₂ ÷ FiO₂ without a line
The baby lung: the open lung is small, so a normal breath is a big one
Strain = VT ÷ aerated lung: the same 6 mL/kg is three times the stretch
Volutrauma · atelectrauma · barotrauma · biotrauma
Driving pressure = plateau − PEEP: keep it ≤ 15
Stress index: a straight rise is right; bending up means over-distension

Recap · Protective settings

Part 2

PEEP: the ARDSNet table or above, then titrate to the best compliance
Staircase up, then down · R/I ≥ 0.5: a recruiter, go higher; below it, prone early
Volume or pressure: either, if the limits hold · read the exhaled VT every hour
Accept the gas: SpO₂ 92–97 (88–92 if severe) · pH ≥ 7.20 · FiO₂ ≤ 0.6 once PEEP is right

Defining PARDS

Figure

Stress and strain

Gattinoni
Stress = specific elastance × strain
Stress: the pressure across the lung (transpulmonary pressure), not the airway pressure
Strain: the change in volume ÷ the resting lung (FRC); the baby lung makes the same VT a bigger strain
Specific lung elastance is about 13.5 cmH₂O: a strain of 1 means about 13.5 cmH₂O of stress
Injury in models rises steeply once strain passes about 1.5–2: total lung capacity is near 2
Static strain (PEEP volume) is tolerated better than dynamic strain (the tidal breath)
Chiumello et al, AJRCCM 2008 · Protti et al, AJRCCM 2011 · Gattinoni, Intensive Care Med 2016

Stress = specific elastance × strain

Figure

Mechanical power

Ergotrauma
MP (J/min) = 0.098 × RR × VT (L) × (Ppeak − ½ ΔP)
The energy delivered to the lung every minute: pressure, volume, flow and rate together
Rate counts: halving VT but doubling the rate does not halve the power
Adults: power above about 17 J/min linked to higher mortality
Children: index it (per kg or per lung size); higher indexed power tracks with mortality
Latest: power normalised to aerated lung, and the share that is truly damaging (above a threshold)
Gattinoni et al, ICM 2016 · Serpa Neto et al, ICM 2018 · Bhalla et al, PCCM 2022

Driving pressure and mortality

Figure

Oesophageal pressure

Transpulmonary pressure
PL = Paw − Pes
A balloon catheter in the lower oesophagus estimates pleural pressure
End-expiration: set PEEP so PL is 0 to +5 · alveoli stay open
End-inspiration: keep PL below about 20–25 cmH₂O · no over-distension
Most useful when the chest wall is stiff: obesity, abdominal distension, oedema, burns
EPVent-2 (2019): Pes-guided PEEP no better than a high PEEP table overall
Talmor et al, NEJM 2008 · Beitler et al, JAMA 2019 (EPVent-2) · Understanding transpulmonary pressure

Driving pressure: transpulmonary and chest wall parts

Figure

Electrical impedance tomography

EIT · bedside
HowA belt of 16–32 electrodesTiny currents, no radiationA live image of where each breath goes
What it showsVentral vs dorsal ventilationCollapse and over-distension, region by regionPendelluft and the effect of prone
PEEP by EITStep PEEP downCollapse rises, over-distension fallsSet PEEP near the crossing
Costa et al, ICM 2009 · Frerichs et al, Thorax 2017 (TREND consensus)

Why prone works

Mechanisms
The pleural pressure gradient evens out: dorsal lung opens, ventral lung stops over-stretching
Lung and chest wall shapes match better: more homogeneous ventilation, less stress and strain
Perfusion stays dorsal while ventilation moves there: better V/Q, less shunt
The heart and abdomen no longer press on the dorsal lung
Secretions drain; the RV is unloaded as PVR falls and PaCO₂ improves
Guérin et al, ICM 2020 (review) · Gattinoni et al, AJRCCM 2013
